_comment: ORDER SETS / PROTOCOLS: site-configurable clinical content.
Every set below is a STARTER. The drug choices, especially the empirical
antibiotic, are the ones a general medical ward in India would most often
reach for, and they are NOT a substitute for this hospital's own antibiotic
policy, microbiology advice, or formulary. Edit this file to match local
policy, restart Orb, and the ward sees the change.
Every set MUST cite the guideline it encodes. A protocol with no provenance
is deleted by the first consultant who disagrees with it, and rightly so.
A medication item names drug_name / dose / route / frequency SEPARATELY from
its description, because the dose guard reads those fields. Writing the dose
only into the prose would leave the guard nothing to check.

sets.name: Sepsis Six (1-hour bundle)
sets.indication: Suspected sepsis: NEWS2 5 or more, or any red-flag sepsis criterion.

guideline.name: Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2021: 1-hour bundle; UK Sepsis Trust 'Sepsis Six'
guideline.citation: Evans L, Rhodes A, Alhazzani W, et al. Surviving Sepsis Campaign: International Guidelines for Management of Sepsis and Septic Shock 2021. Crit Care Med 2021;49(11):e1063-e1143.
guideline.reviewed_by: SITE TO COMPLETE: name the consultant who signed this set off

items.description: Serum lactate
Blood culture, two sets: BEFORE the first antibiotic dose
Full blood count
Creatinine and electrolytes
Oxygen, titrated to SpO2 94-98% (88-92% if at risk of hypercapnia)
Ceftriaxone 2 g IV: first dose STAT, after cultures are drawn
items.note: EMPIRICAL CHOICE: replace with this hospital's own antibiotic policy for suspected sepsis of unknown source.

items.description: Sodium chloride 0.9% 500 mL IV over 15 minutes; reassess and repeat to 30 mL/kg if hypotensive
Measure hourly urine output: catheterise if not passing urine
Repeat NEWS2 observations hourly for 6 hours

sets.name: Acute coronary syndrome: initial management
sets.indication: Ischaemic-sounding chest pain with ECG change or a raised troponin.

guideline.name: ESC 2023 Guidelines for the management of acute coronary syndromes
guideline.citation: Byrne RA, Rossello X, Coughlan JJ, et al. 2023 ESC Guidelines for the management of acute coronary syndromes. Eur Heart J 2023;44(38):3720-3826.
guideline.reviewed_by: SITE TO COMPLETE: name the consultant who signed this set off

items.description: 12-lead ECG within 10 minutes of arrival; repeat if pain recurs
High-sensitivity cardiac troponin I, baseline sample
Full blood count
Creatinine and electrolytes
Aspirin 300 mg orally, chewed, loading dose
Clopidogrel 300 mg orally, loading dose
items.note: Confirm against the local antiplatelet policy and the planned reperfusion strategy before giving.

items.description: Glyceryl trinitrate 500 micrograms sublingual, repeat after 5 minutes if pain persists and systolic BP is above 90 mmHg
Morphine 2.5 mg IV, titrated to pain
Atorvastatin 80 mg orally at night
Portable chest X-ray
Continuous cardiac monitoring until pain-free and troponin trend known

sets.name: Diabetic ketoacidosis: first hour
sets.indication: Capillary ketones 3.0 mmol/L or above, or urine ketones 2+ or more, with glucose above 11 mmol/L and acidosis.

guideline.name: Joint British Diabetes Societies for Inpatient Care: The Management of Diabetic Ketoacidosis in Adults
guideline.citation: Joint British Diabetes Societies for Inpatient Care. The Management of Diabetic Ketoacidosis in Adults (3rd edition, 2023). See also: American Diabetes Association, Standards of Care in Diabetes.
guideline.reviewed_by: SITE TO COMPLETE: name the consultant who signed this set off

items.description: Capillary blood ketones (beta-hydroxybutyrate): repeat hourly
Venous blood gas for pH and bicarbonate. Repeat at 1 hour, then 2-hourly
Serum glucose
Creatinine and electrolytes: potassium guides replacement
Sodium chloride 0.9% 1000 mL IV over 1 hour
Insulin (soluble human) fixed-rate IV infusion at 0.1 units/kg/hour
items.note: Weight-based rate. Orb's dose guard declines to judge per-kg-per-hour rates and says so. The prescriber owns this number.

items.description: Potassium chloride 40 mmol added to each litre of IV fluid, adjusted to serum potassium. Diluted and infused, never by IV push.
items.note: Withhold if serum potassium is above 5.5 mmol/L.

items.description: Hourly capillary blood glucose
Hourly fluid balance: catheterise if no urine passed within 60 minutes
Continue the patient's usual long-acting basal insulin at the usual dose

sets.name: Routine post-operative care (adult, ward)
sets.indication: Adult returning to a general ward after uncomplicated surgery.

guideline.name: ERAS Society perioperative care guidelines; WHO Surgical Safety Checklist
guideline.citation: ERAS Society. Guidelines for Perioperative Care (procedure-specific series), https://erassociety.org/guidelines/. World Health Organization. WHO Surgical Safety Checklist, 2009.
guideline.reviewed_by: SITE TO COMPLETE: name the consultant who signed this set off

items.description: NEWS2 observations every 30 minutes for 2 hours, then hourly for 4 hours, then 4-hourly
Paracetamol 1 g every 6 hours, maximum 4 g in 24 hours
Morphine 2.5 mg IV every 2 hours as required for severe pain
Ondansetron 4 mg IV every 8 hours as required for nausea
Enoxaparin 40 mg subcutaneously once daily for VTE prophylaxis, starting 6-12 hours after surgery
items.note: Withhold if actively bleeding, if the surgeon has asked for it to be held, or if creatinine clearance is below 30 mL/min without dose adjustment.

items.description: Full blood count on the first post-operative morning
Check the wound site and record drain output once per shift
Sit out of bed and mobilise on day 0 if safe to do so

sets.name: Acute severe asthma (adult)
sets.indication: Acute asthma with PEF below 50% predicted, or any life-threatening feature.

guideline.name: BTS/SIGN 158 British guideline on the management of asthma; GINA report
guideline.citation: British Thoracic Society / Scottish Intercollegiate Guidelines Network. SIGN 158: British guideline on the management of asthma, 2019. Global Initiative for Asthma. Global Strategy for Asthma Management and Prevention.
guideline.reviewed_by: SITE TO COMPLETE: name the consultant who signed this set off

items.description: Oxygen, titrated to SpO2 94-98%
Salbutamol 5 mg nebulised, driven by oxygen. Repeat every 15-20 minutes, or continuously if life-threatening
Ipratropium bromide 500 micrograms nebulised every 4-6 hours
Prednisolone 40 mg orally once daily for 5 days
items.note: Use hydrocortisone 100 mg IV instead if the oral route is not available.

items.description: Arterial blood gas if SpO2 is below 92% or any life-threatening feature is present
Portable chest X-ray only if pneumothorax or consolidation is suspected, or the patient fails to respond
Continuous pulse oximetry, target SpO2 94-98%
Record peak expiratory flow before and after each nebuliser
Escalate to critical care if PEF is below 33% predicted, the patient is exhausted, or PaCO2 is rising
